$comment: The Almanac (design doc §7): the permanent tree bought with Verdure, surviving every Migration. Verdure is never spent away — nodes ALLOCATE from the banked total (available = verdurePoints - sum of owned node costs) so the +2%/pt passive keeps counting the full total. All costs and effect sizes are first guesses tuned to ~10 Verdure from the first Migration. requires = single prerequisite node. repeatable = the line is bought over and over, level L costing costVerdure · costGrowth.almanac^L, its effects scaled by the levels held; every other node is a one-off. The exotic lines (grantUpgrade / keepCraftOrders) act at the fold: they scale the ladder RE-CLIMB downward with the fold count — the half of the pacing fix no yield knob delivers. A grantUpgrade of a trail map must have its zone's requiredTool covered by a tool rung granted in its own requires chain (validator-enforced), or the grant would sit inert forever.

nodes.name: The Long Song
nodes.$note: The endless line — the Almanac's only repeatable node, and the reason Verdure never dead-ends. The rest of the tree totals 178 points (99 before the exotic lines and the kept things), which a steady warden passes within a handful of folds; after that the currency kept arriving with nothing to spend it on, which is what made a late fold feel like it had nothing in it. Level L costs costVerdure · costGrowth.almanac^L forever. It grants the SAME additive value to gathering and to carrying on purpose: yieldBonus and carrierCapacityBonus are both summed bands (yield is mult·(1+bonus), haul is haulMult·(1+carrierBonus)), so every level moves the two by the same proportion and the gather-vs-haul ratio cannot drift. Granting the gathering half alone would re-open the full-basket jam that the self-haul floor was built to catch.
